data.title: Linux containers explained (mock fixture)
data.text:
Linux containers explained

A container is an ordinary Linux process that the kernel isolates using namespaces and cgroups.
Namespaces give the process its own view of process IDs, mounts, network interfaces and hostnames.
Control groups (cgroups) limit how much CPU, memory and how many process IDs a container may use.
Because containers share the host kernel, a kernel vulnerability can let a process escape the container.
Dropping Linux capabilities and enabling no-new-privileges reduces what a compromised process can do.

data.title: gVisor overview (mock fixture)
data.text:
gVisor overview

gVisor is an application kernel, written in Go, that implements a substantial portion of the Linux system call interface.
It provides an additional layer of isolation between running applications and the host operating system.
gVisor includes an OCI runtime called runsc that integrates with Docker and Kubernetes.
Workloads that make many system calls can run slower under gVisor than under the default runc runtime.
